title: Chapter 11 — Laundry
intro: Front load vs. top load, capacity truths, pedestals and stacking, and dryer technology.

sections.title: The Great Debate
sections.content:
Front load versus top load is one of the most common customer questions. Both have legitimate advantages.

Front load: better cleaning performance, more water efficient, higher spin speeds reduce drying time, stackable. Top load: no bending, familiar, generally less expensive, faster cycle times on some models.

The right answer depends on the customer's priorities — not on which one you prefer. Discovery determines the recommendation.

sections.title: Capacity and Stacking
sections.content:
Customers overestimate how much capacity they need or underestimate it entirely. Ask about household size and laundry frequency instead of letting them guess at cubic feet.

Stacking is a space solution with trade-offs — dryer access is higher, capacity may be limited, ventilation requirements change. Know the requirements before recommending it.

sections.title: Dryer Technology
sections.content:
Electric versus gas is determined by the home's hookup. Heat pump dryers are the emerging technology — lower temperature, gentler on clothes, more energy efficient, but longer cycle times. Ventless options matter for condos and apartments.

Know what is available in each technology and who it fits.

sections.title: Coaching Rule
sections.content:
When evaluating laundry knowledge, ask:

Can the salesperson explain the pros and cons of front load vs. top load without bias?
Do they ask about the home's hookup before recommending a dryer?
Do they understand stacking and ventless requirements?
Do they match capacity to household size — not just customer assumptions?
